🏜️ Sand-dune cheat sheet
Open daylight hours. Sandboard/sled rentals run about $25 each, first-come first-served, returned 30 min before the visitor center closes. Hours shift with daylight — the one Friday timing detail worth checking that week.

Why it could be perfect
The novelty is the hike. You're walking the river between canyon walls — no summit or chains required.
Why it's still work
Uneven, slippery river rocks. Balance. Current. Wet feet and legs. Not a flat stroll.

Size-14 boot situation ✅

Good news: Zion Outfitter carries canyoneering boots through men's US 15. The warm-weather package (about $35) includes boots, neoprene socks, and a wooden hiking stick. Reserved customers are guaranteed sizes if picked up before 10 AM.

Best move: reserve both sets and pick them up Friday evening (typically 4 PM until an hour before closing, based on availability).

Reserve Narrows gear Official Narrows page Check Zion conditions
⚠️ The morning-of safety check
Check official Zion conditions and the flash-flood forecast. Narrows conditions change and the hike can close. If it's closed, pivot to a beautiful easy-hike Zion day and keep the hot springs plan.

Day 05 · Sunday
Choose your own adventure
Day 05 — Sunday, Sep 13

Bryce? Then Vegas.

🗺️ Bryce → Vegas

Tap how you're feeling — the guide tells you what kind of day that is.

Go to Bryce. Spend 1–2 hours in the amphitheater: Sunrise Point → the paved 0.5-mile Rim Trail → Sunset Point → Inspiration Point if you want one more overlook. Back to the hotel, reset, then Vegas.
Bryce is still doable — keep it tiny. Drive up, see the main amphitheater overlooks, skip a real hike, come back to Springdale and rest before Vegas.
Skip Bryce with zero guilt. Sleep, coffee, pool/hot tub, maybe one easy Zion walk. Leave for Vegas feeling like humans.

Bryce NPS recommends the amphitheater for visitors with only 1–3 hours; the paved Sunrise-to-Sunset section is 1 mile round trip and rated easy.

Where to eat

Good food, easy prices

Local favorites that are well-loved and won't wreck the budget. All of them have solid dairy-free options, so you're covered — no need to overthink it.

Sedona

Indian Gardens Cafe & Market 🥪Casual · $$ · the local darling

A shaded creekside garden patio up Oak Creek Canyon. Great sandwiches, salads, and coffee — a perennial top-rated spot and a lovely low-key lunch.

Wildflower Bread CompanyCasual · $ · fast & reliable

Order-at-the-counter bakery cafe with big salads, sandwiches, and red-rock views from the patio. Easy, cheap, consistently good.

Picazzo's Organic ItalianSit-down · $$ · crowd-pleaser

Pizza and pasta done well, with a whole dedicated vegan/gluten-free menu — so it's an easy dinner where everyone's happy.

Rocky RD Ice Cream Co. 🍦Dessert · $ · the sweet stop

Excellent scoop shop with genuinely great non-dairy sorbets (prickly-pear lime, mangonada). Closed Wednesdays, so make it a Thursday treat.

Element breakfastFree · already paid for

Hot breakfast 6:30–9:30 AM at the hotel. Use it — it makes the hike mornings effortless.

Springdale / Zion

Oscar's Cafe 🍳Sit-down · $$ · post-hike hero

The classic Springdale after-Zion meal — big portions, great patio, burgers/Mexican/veggie plates. Reliably one of the highest-rated in town.

Deep Creek Coffee Co. 🍵Coffee/breakfast · $ · early birds

Opens 6 AM with coffee, breakfast burritos and baked goods, plus online pre-order — perfect fuel before the 7 AM shuttle.

Zion Canyon Brew PubSit-down · $$ · right at the gate

Casual pub food and a big patio literally at the park entrance — an easy, scenic spot to land after the Narrows.

Sol Foods MarketGrab-and-go · $ · trail fuel

Deli sandwiches, snacks, and water to stock the room and the daypack before Saturday.

Scout Bar & GrillIn your hotel · $$ · zero effort

Inside Red Cliffs Lodge, breakfast through dinner. The "we are not getting back in the car" option for the Saturday reset.

Las Vegas

Keep it simple, keep it cheap 🎰Casual · one short night

With a 6:15 AM flight, skip the big reservation. Grab an in-n-out-style bite or a fun food-hall stop near the W/Mandalay Bay, see the Bellagio fountains, and get a ridiculous dessert on the Strip.

Sunrise + sunset

Where the light is worth chasing

No need to chase every sunrise. Florida body-clock jet lag may hand you an early morning for free.

🌅
Sedona sunrise
Bell Rock / Courthouse Butte if you wake early — easy to pair with your Thursday hike.
🌄
Sedona sunset
Airport Mesa for the classic panorama. Doe Mountain for a short hike with an "earned" view.
🏜️
Coral Pink golden hour
Friday's later arrival is a feature — softer light gives the dune ridges more texture and color.
🏞️
Zion evening
No sunset hike Saturday — you already have the 7 PM hot springs. Let the soak be the evening event.
🧡
Bryce sunrise?
Beautiful, not required. If you want sleep, go later and enjoy the amphitheater in normal morning light.
Rule: one beautiful light moment beats an alarm every morning.
